newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Elpo to enter bourse free market on Feb 20.
newsitem.headline: Polish Elpo to enter bourse free market on Feb 20.

text.p: Polish jeans garment maker Elpo SA, the first company to enter the Warsaw exchange's so far dormant free market for small and less liquid firms, will enter the bourse on February 20, the bourse president said on Friday.
"The management of the bourse will introduce 746,960 shares of Elpo on the free market of the bourse, the first listing will take place on the bourse session on February 20," Wieslaw Rozlucki said.
The free market was set up for companies which do not meet listing requirements of the main and parallel markets -- ones with smaller capital and a short audited track record.

The value of shares of a company listed on the free market has to be at least four million zlotys, its book value at least four million, share capital of 1.5 million and the firm has to publish a financial report for the last financial year.

Elpo earlier said it saw its 1997 net profit rising to 2.1 million zlotys, up from last year's 1.3 million. It said its sales were likely to grow to 20.5 million zlotys this year, up from 15 million zlotys in 1996.
